French-American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who currently serves as the [[Coach (basketball)|head coach]] of [[ASVEL Basket|LDLC ASVEL]] of the French [[LNB Élite]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. The son of a basketball pro, Parker started his career at [[Paris Saint-Germain Basketball|PSG-Racing Basket]] in the [[LNB Pro A|French basketball league]] before joining the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was selected by the Spurs with the 28th overall pick in the [[2001 NBA draft]], and quickly became their starting [[point guard]]. Parker won four [[List of NBA champions|NBA championships]] ([[2003 NBA Finals|2003]], [[2005 NBA Finals|2005]], [[2007 NBA Finals|2007]], and [[2014 NBA Finals|2014]]), all of which were with the Spurs. He also played for [[ASVEL Basket]] in France during the [[2011 NBA lockout]], and finished his playing career after one season with the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. He retired as the ninth leading scorer and ranks fifth in career assists in [[NBA playoffs]] history. Parker was named to six [[NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star games]], three [[All-NBA]] Second Teams, an All-NBA Third Team and was named [[NBA Finals Most Valuable Player Award|MVP]] of the [[2007 NBA Finals]]. He was also a member of the All-Rookie First Team and had his No. 9 [[retired number|retired]] by the Spurs. In the summer of 2000, Parker was invited to the [[Nike Hoop Summit]] in [[Indianapolis]]. In a contest between the American and European [[All-Star]]s, Parker recorded 20 [[point (basketball)|points]], seven [[assist (basketball)|assists]], four [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and two [[steal (basketball)|steals]]. His performance prompted a recruiting war among several colleges, including [[UCLA]] and [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]]. Parker decided to forgo the [[NCAA]] and to remain in France; he spent the next year with Paris Basket Racing in the [[LNB Pro A|French League]] before entering the [[2001 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last1=Taylor |first1=Phil |title=Avant-Guard Raised in France and only 19, Spurs rookie playmaker Tony Parker is way ahead of the game, running the team like a seasoned pro |url=https://vault.si.com/vault/2001/12/10/avant-guard-raised-in-france-and-only-19-spurs-rookie-playmaker-tony-parker-is-way-ahead-of-the-game-running-the-team-like-a-seasoned-pro |website=Sports Illustrated |access-date=5 November 2025 |date=10 December 2001}} === San Antonio Spurs (2001–2011) === ==== First championship (2002–2003) ==== {{Quote box| width=40% | align=right | quote="''...[When] we gave [Tony Parker] his first workout, we didn't think he was tough enough – and we sent him home. And then we set up another interview, another workout... and he was fantastic in that one.''" | source=-[[Gregg Popovich]], after the 2007 championship''Wire Services''. "Spurs Coach: I didn't like him", The New Paper, 24 June 2007 }} Before the [[2001 NBA draft]], Parker was invited to the [[San Antonio Spurs]]' summer camp. Coach [[Gregg Popovich]] had him play against Spurs scout and ex-NBA player [[Lance Blanks]]. Parker was overwhelmed by Blanks's tough and physical defense, and Popovich was ready to send him away after just 10 minutes.{{Citation|last=Hieronimi|first=Jan|title=FIVE|date=September–October 2007|newspaper=FIVE magazine|pages=36–39}} But after seeing a "best of" mix tape of Parker's best plays, Popovich decided to invite Parker a second time.[http://www.jockbio.com/Bios/Parker/Parker_bio.html Tony Parker Bio] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080207125133/http://www.jockbio.com/Bios/Parker/Parker_bio.html |date=7 February 2008 }}, jockbio.com, Retrieved 28 January 2008 This time, Parker made a better impression against Blanks; the Frenchman later described Blanks as a "one-man wrecking crew". But while Popovich decided that Parker was worth the gamble, the Spurs still had to hope that other teams would not pick Parker during the draft. Parker's name was barely mentioned in the pre-draft predictions, and the point guard was drafted 28th overall by the Spurs on draft day. After initially playing backup to [[Antonio Daniels]], Parker became a starter and made 77 regular-season appearances in his rookie season, averaging 9.2 [[point (basketball)|points]], 4.3 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] and 2.6 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] in 29.4 minutes per game. When he played against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on 30 October 2001, he became the third French player to play in an NBA game, after [[Tariq Abdul-Wahad]] and [[Jérome Moïso|Jérôme Moïso]].Friedman, Brad, [http://www.nba.com/fedex/eng/france.html "Depth of Talent and Promise Impressive Out of France"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080626103802/http://www.nba.com/fedex/eng/france.html |date=26 June 2008 }}, nba.com, accessed 5 February 2008 By the end of the season, the rookie led San Antonio in assists and [[steal (basketball)|steals]], and was named to the All-Rookie First Team for [[2001–02 NBA season|2001–02]], becoming the first foreign-born [[Point guard|guard]] to earn the honor. In 2002–03, Parker played in all 82 regular-season games as San Antonio's starting [[point guard]][http://www.nba.com/playerfile/tony_parker/career_stats.html Tony Parker Info Page – Career Stats and Totals] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070217120015/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/tony_parker/career_stats.html |date=17 February 2007}}, nba.com, Retrieved 14 June 2007 on a team that was largely revamped from previous years. He improved his regular season statistics, averaging 15.5 [[points per game]] (ppg), 5.3 assists per game (apg) and 2.6 [[rebounds per game]] (rpg). Parker's role as the team's [[playmaker]] was reflected in his leading the team in assists on 49 occasions. During the 2003 [[NBA All-Star Weekend]], Parker represented the Sophomores in the [[Rookie Challenge]], and also participated in the inaugural [[NBA All-Star Weekend Skills Challenge|Skills Challenge]]. [[2003 NBA Playoffs|In the post season]], the Spurs, led by Tim Duncan, defeated the [[New Jersey Nets]] 4–2 in [[2003 NBA Finals|the finals]], and Parker earned his first NBA [[championship ring]].[http://www.nba.com/history/finals/champions.html NBA Finals: All-Time Champions] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170817094310/http://www.nba.com/history/finals/champions.html |date=17 August 2017 }}, nba.com, accessed 4 May 2007 Despite the victory, Parker struggled with inconsistent play throughout the playoffs, and was often benched in favor of more experienced guards [[Steve Kerr]] and [[Speedy Claxton]] late in the games. ==== Second championship (2003–2005) ==== Despite winning a championship with the Spurs, doubts lingered over Parker's future. The Spurs had attempted and failed to acquire [[New Jersey Nets]]' [[Jason Kidd]], but Parker told coach Popovich that he wanted to be San Antonio's starting point guard.Wetzel, Dan, [https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=dw-parker061507&prov=yhoo&type=lgns "French connection"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071007201852/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=dw-parker061507&prov=yhoo&type=lgns |date=7 October 2007 }}, sports.yahoo.com, 14 June 2007, Retrieved 30 September 2007 Parker played well during [[2003–04 NBA season|the regular season]], recording 14.7 ppg, 5.5 apg and 3.2 rpg. However, the Spurs were defeated by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the [[Western Conference (NBA)|Western Conference]] semi-finals in the [[2004 NBA Playoffs]], and were denied back-to-back titles. Prior to the start of the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]], Parker signed a six-year, $66 million contract extension through the 2010–11 season.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/columns/story?columnist=stein_marc&id=1916856|title='Teemy' holds team together|date=5 November 2004 |access-date=June 5, 2025}} On the year, he would once again record improved regular season statistics, tallying 16.6 ppg, 6.1 apg and a career-high 3.7 rpg. He was also ranked 13th in the league in total assists, and was third among point guards in [[field goal percentage]]. The Spurs were strong in [[2005 NBA Playoffs|the playoffs]], and Parker was instrumental in the victories over the [[Denver Nuggets]], [[Seattle SuperSonics]] and [[Phoenix Suns]]. However, Parker struggled in the Finals series against the [[Detroit Pistons]]. Spurs colleagues [[Manu Ginóbili]] and [[Brent Barry]] often took over playmaking duties as Parker was unable to perform as well as he did in the regular season. Nevertheless, the Spurs won their third-ever NBA championship by defeating the defending champions 4–3 in the [[2005 NBA Finals]]. {{Quote box | width = 30% | align = left | quote = ''"He told me, 'Coach, I'll play in the NBA and, one day, France will recognize me as a great player'. It's incredible how, at 18 years old, he could have such confidence. I thought he could play in the NBA, but not that he would become a player of the importance he is today."'' | source = -Claude Bergeaud, who coached Parker on the French junior team }} ==== Third championship (2005–2007) ==== [[File:Tony parker spurs vs wizards.jpg|thumb|Parker in a 2007–08 game against Washington Wizards' [[Gilbert Arenas]]]] Parker was selected for the first time in his career an [[NBA All-Star]] for the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]][http://www.nba.com/games/20060219/ESTWST/boxscore.html Boxscore] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090316065709/http://www.nba.com/games/20060219/ESTWST/boxscore.html |date=16 March 2009 }}, nba.com, 19 February 2006, accessed 4 May 2007 as he managed 18.9 ppg and an impressive .548 in field goal percentage. Parker's scoring average was even higher than Duncan's,[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/tim_duncan/career_stats.html Tim Duncan – Career Stats and Totals] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141013114615/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/tim_duncan/career_stats.html |date=13 October 2014}}, nba.com, accessed 2 October 2007 and his form propelled the Spurs to a 63–19 win–loss record and qualification for the [[2006 NBA Playoffs]]. It was the Spurs 13th straight 50 win season (a new NBA record) despite the lockout-shortened season.{{cite web |last1=O'Connell |first1=Ryan |title=2012/13 NBA season previews: San Antonio Spurs |url=https://www.theroar.com.au/2012/10/29/201213-nba-season-previews-san-antonio-spurs/ |website=Roar |access-date=4 November 2025 |date=28 October 2012}} On 4 February 2012, Parker became the all-time assist leader of the franchise with 4,477, surpassing [[Avery Johnson]], adding 42 points in a victory against [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].[http://www.cbssports.com/mcc/blogs/entry/22748484/34706507 "Parker becomes Spurs all-time assists leader] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140523230345/http://www.cbssports.com/mcc/blogs/entry/22748484/34706507 |date=23 May 2014}}, cbssports.com, 5 February 2012, Retrieved 23 May 2012 Parker received his fourth [[2012 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star]] nod and finished fifth in [[NBA Most Valuable Player Award|MVP]] award voting, receiving four first-place votes.{{cite web |title=2011-12 NBA Awards Voting |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/awards/awards_2012.html |website=Basketball Reference |access-date=4 November 2025}} In the [[2012 NBA Playoffs]], the Spurs swept their first two opponents, the Utah Jazz and Los Angeles Clippers, to reach the Western Conference Finals against the Oklahoma City Thunder. In his 17th and final season with the Spurs, Parker played 55 games and averaged a career-low 7.7 points a game. Parker is considered the Spurs' greatest point guard and left as the franchise's assist leader with 6,829.{{cite web |last1=Spears |first1=Marc J. |title='Merci, Tony': Spurs honor Tony Parker in ceremony to retire No. 9 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28062465/merci-tony-spurs-honor-tony-parker-ceremony-no-9-jersey |website=ESPN.com |access-date=12 November 2019 |date=11 November 2019 |archive-date=12 November 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191112081827/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28062465/merci-tony-spurs-honor-tony-parker-ceremony-no-9-jersey |url-status=live }} === Charlotte Hornets (2018–2019) === On 23 July 2018, Parker signed a two-year, $10 million contract with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/hornets-sign-free-agent-guard-tony-parker|title=Hornets Sign Free-Agent Guard Tony Parker|work=NBA.com|date=23 July 2018|access-date=23 July 2018|archive-date=28 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201128213940/https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/hornets-sign-free-agent-guard-tony-parker|url-status=live}} He made his debut as a Hornets player on 17 October 2018, recording 8 points on 4/8 shooting, 7 assists, and 3 rebounds while coming off of the bench in 19 minutes of action in a 113–112 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/nba/charlotte-hornets/article220198650.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181103224110/https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/nba/charlotte-hornets/article220198650.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 November 2018|title=A dilemma with Tony Parker's stellar Hornets debut? He was voted by his peers in a 2007 poll as one of the quickest players in the NBA.[http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2007/players/02/20/poll.0220/index.html SI Players Poll] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110622092140/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2007/players/02/20/poll.0220/index.html |date=22 June 2011 }}, sportsillustrated.cnn.com, 20 February 2007, accessed 20 April 2007 Parker often [[Slasher (basketball)|slashed]] to the basket for [[layup]]s, and the [[teardrop (basketball)|teardrop]] was considered his "signature shot". Despite his relatively small size for a basketball player, he led the league in "points in the paint" for the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]].{{cite web |last1=Dizon |first1=Orel |title=Tony Parker on the key to leading the league in points in the paint: "It's all about the teardrop" |url=https://www.basketballnetwork.net/old-school/tony-parker-on-the-key-to-leading-the-league-in-points-in-the-paint |website=Basketball Network |access-date=6 November 2025 |date=30 November 2023}} In the initial part of his NBA career, Parker was considered an erratic shooter off the ball. During the 2005 offseason, Coach [[Gregg Popovich|Popovich]] decided to work on that aspect of his play. Spurs shooting coach [[Chip Engelland]] forbade Parker to shoot any three-point shots and corrected his shooting motion and his thumb position. As a result, by the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]], Parker's accuracy rose by 4% (field goals and three-point shots). He was also able to connect on 78% of his free throws that season.
